head: AT&T landline shutdown starts November 15, Verizon copper on November 16
dek: AT&T is allowed to start shutting off old copper landlines in parts of 18 US states from November 15, and Verizon starts similar steps in 8 states on November 16. DSL internet over the same copper lines is being retired too.
details: The FCC approval for AT&T covers parts of more than 1,000 local service areas and about 90,000 remaining customers, including 53 communities in Louisiana. AT&T's states are Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and Wisconsin; Verizon's are Florida, Indiana, Minnesota, Nebraska, Nevada, North Carolina, Texas and Wisconsin. It happens area by area, not all at once, and affected customers get a letter first. Verizon says it won't cut service where no adequate replacement is available.
where: Parts of 18 US states (AT&T) from November 15 and 8 states (Verizon) from November 16, area by area
means: If you still have an AT&T or Verizon landline or DSL on copper, your line may stop working on the date in your letter. Alarms, fax machines and medical monitors on that line need a new connection too.
todo: Look for the letter from your provider and check its date. Compare the replacements: AT&T offers Phone - Advanced, which keeps your number and existing home phones (not rotary phones) and has 24-hour battery backup for 911, plus fiber and wireless plans; Verizon offers fiber, fixed wireless and 5G home phone. Switch before the date, and check on older neighbors who still use a landline.
